astronomy_picture_of_the_day.title: Auroras from Space
astronomy_picture_of_the_day.explanation: What do auroras look like from above? Behold!  From the ground, auroras dance high above clouds, frequently causing spectacular displays.  From space, they look a bit different. As the International Space Station (ISS) circles the Earth every 90 minutes, it sometimes sees auroras below that are active on the night side.
